title: What AI Tool for a developer with a programming background?
author: kiapakaru
selftext:
I have used github copilot in the past and it served me quite well. As i am able to describe what i want and how i want it implemented, i never had problems  with tokens or the urge to use the most expensive models. However my weakness lies in my artistic skills, creating good assets and making nice ui/ux polish

I have never used claude code or codex yet and as im about to subscribe to any of the three for a month, im thinking about which to choose.

Are claude code/ codex worth it when it comes to asset generation and how do they compare with the usage cost? Something im maybe missing that i should consider?

comments.author: _raydeStar
comments.body: newer opus and astra are both incredible at helping you work.  Warning though -- Blender and unreal work are both token hogs.  Not sure about unity or godot.

replies.author: BHTAelitepwn
replies.body: Godot isnt too bad in my experience. Blender is though.

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body: If aesthetics are you concern, I'd give codex a pass and go for claude. Astra's sense of style is grandma underpants compared to claude's luxury lingerie.

replies.author: kiapakaru
replies.body: Haha, thats good to know. Then maybe i should look into claude

comments.author: SlightOfHand_
comments.body: Claude doesn’t have native generation built in, but it can help you set up asset generation. Codex has built in image generation and editing which is pretty useful.

comments.author: GridIron-Grit
comments.body:
Claude. 

And my number one tip is make sure to setup and be disciplined with your GIT repo.

replies.author: kiapakaru
replies.body: Wdym exactly? The versioning itself (smaller commits etc.) or proper integration of markdown files and instructions?

comments.author: vagonblog
comments.body:
if your main goal is generating assets and polishing ui, neither claude code nor codex is a magic replacement for a design tool. they’re much better at writing the code, wiring assets into the project, and iterating on a design you can already describe.

i’d probably try claude code first for visual iteration and frontend work, then use whichever feels better with your workflow. keep github copilot around if it already works well for you, and judge by how quickly you can go from idea to a working result rather than token limits alone.

replies.author: kiapakaru
replies.body: Thank you for your input. I think i will go this way.

comments.author: liatris4405
comments.body:
I've been using AI to develop a game for about three or four months now, and at this point I've reached a personal conclusion: the key to making games with AI is combining multiple services.

If you're making a small and simple game, it's fairly easy. But at the moment, I don't think it's really possible to make a game that looks genuinely decent using just one AI service. What I do think is possible, however, is making a decent-looking game by combining multiple AI tools and services.

When it comes to asset generation, ChatGPT is probably one of the best generative AI tools available right now because it can generate images. However, one thing you need to keep in mind is that ChatGPT-generated images can still be recognizable as AI-generated at a glance.

Claude Code is at a disadvantage in that respect because it doesn't have its own image-generation capability. However, you can give it reference images and have it work with Blender, and it's capable of creating relatively simple low-poly props and environments.

My game development workflow looks something like this:

1. Have ChatGPT or Claude build the basic game systems. This requires giving the AI instructions dozens of times and constantly checking what it produces. You can't just give it a single prompt and expect it to build the entire system correctly.
2. Use Claude or ChatGPT to create the basic environments and background objects. Start by creating things like houses, castles, and other environmental objects. You should also have the AI handle the basic visual setup, including things like shading and lighting.
3. Use external services to generate the assets required by the game. I mainly use Tripo and Meshy to generate 3D characters and objects. When asking a service like Tripo to create a 3D model, use ChatGPT's image-generation feature to create a four-view character reference sheet first. For characters, it's usually a good idea to generate the reference in a T-pose. You can then use that image as the reference for the 3D generation process.
4. For sound effects, use existing CC0 or similar assets whenever possible. If you really can't find the sound effect you need, use an external AI service such as EventLabs to generate it.
5. For background music, use an AI music-generation service such as Suno.
6. Have the AI combine everything from steps 1–5, and then keep polishing the game over and over again. From that point on, it's basically an endless cycle of iteration and refinement. Whenever you realize you're missing an asset, use one of the services above to create it, integrate it into the game, and continue polishing.

I also only have programming experience and can't create art or music myself, but by following this workflow, I'm now starting to put together a reasonably decent game.

comments.author: stjimmy96
comments.body:
In the same boat and I would say that your main problem is that none of these AI tools can give you an art direction. Claude Code with Blender MC or even by coding the models directly (for simpler visual styles) does a great job at implementing, but the vision is still yours. 

Normally in game development you would create some concept art first, and only then translate it to an actual model. But coherent concept art is the most creative part of this process and it’s something AI can’t really do.

replies.author: kiapakaru
replies.body: I agree. It is becoming difficult when you have a certain art direction in mind but dont have the skills to flesh it out. I know that this is basically a skill gap which i try to smallen using ai. Making concept art is defenitly a good idea though as they can then feed as reference againt

replies.author: Nilo_Team
replies.body: for the 3D side neither claude nor codex really gens meshes - you'd pair one with a 3D gen. nilo.io does text or image to 3D in the browser, so your concept art can be the ref, then model settings + LOD slider to keep polys sane and export GLB/FBX. auto-rig works if chars are bipedal T-pose. free plan has weekly usage

comments.author: VastReception1347
comments.body: Codex has imagegen skill that can be used to generate textures and sprites, works quite well, I must admit. Claude on the other side is imo better in coding but lack any image generation skill and can only produce some vector graphics using python and image transformation on top.

comments.author: Big_Whale_95
comments.body:
Claude + T3 Code (open source and free) 

Thank me later 😅

comments.author: Iaghlim
comments.body:
I've been working with unity + AI for the past 11 months

Every month things gets better, havent releases no games yet since i'm building a complex online one

I've tried bezi, cursor, antigravity, codex and devin

For a long time, cursor was the main working horse, most of coding system was implemented with composer AMD reviewed by me + opus

Lately, codex has been a great help but i'm not working with code mainly anymore, right now im using it to help me with Animations debug, tools in unity to help me building stuff, enhancements with splines and etc

I'd say, if your main concern is coding only, go for the ones that give you more usage, cursor was the one for a long time, now, maybe luna 6 or devin with swe unlimited(temporary)

With a good coding background, simplier models will be able to help you a lot if you properly prepare the ground for it

If you really want to vibe code it, then you have to pay more for the premium models

comments.author: JDad67
comments.body: 50 years coding. Claude code w/ their desktop app. Opus 5.5 currently (changes often). $100 subscription. Create a directory and point it at it. And tell it what you want.  API/tokens to either fal.ai and/or pixel lab. Have blender installed with the mcp.
